speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a significant medical history and present with gait and limb ataxia; to understand the underlying cause, could you please describe the specific nature of your ataxia and when these symptoms first began?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description. The clumsiness is notably worse on the right side; could you tell me if these symptoms are constant or if they worsen when you look to the right? Also, do you have any history of stroke, head trauma, or a known brain tumor?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: PML (Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy).

Given your history of Crohn's disease and recent treatment with natalizumab, combined with your acute onset of unilateral ataxia and clumsiness, you are at high risk for JC virus reactivation. I need to confirm this immediately.

REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast.
REQUEST IMAGES.
